territorial_scope.description: Applies to the commission's curriculum frameworks and instructional-material criteria under California's Education Code.

evidence.quote: The commission shall consider incorporating AI literacy content into the mathematics, science, and history-social science curriculum frameworks

summary.short: Amends California Education Code § 33548 so the commission shall consider adding AI literacy, media literacy and related content to curriculum frameworks and instructional-material criteria, with timing keyed to revisions after January 1, 2024 or 2025.
summary.long: Amends Education Code § 33548, which defines 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy', 'digital citizenship' and 'media literacy' (subd. (a)). For the English language arts/English language development framework, the commission shall consider, when next revised after January 1, 2024, incorporating the Model Library Standards and media literacy content at each grade level (subd. (b)). For the mathematics, science and history-social science frameworks and related instructional-material criteria, the commission shall consider incorporating media literacy content when those frameworks are next revised or materials next adopted after January 1, 2024 or 2025 (subd. (c)). Subdivision (d) provides that the commission shall consider incorporating AI literacy content into the mathematics, science and history-social science frameworks when those frameworks are next revised after January 1, 2025, and shall consider including AI literacy in its criteria for evaluating instructional materials when those materials are next adopted after January 1, 2025. The operative duties are phrased as 'consider', not as a requirement to adopt. The text states no penalties, enforcement mechanism or private right of action.

relations.note: Bill Section 1 amends Education Code § 33548 (curriculum frameworks and instructional materials; AI literacy, media literacy and Model Library Standards). The target is not in the registry.

notes: Only one amended section (Education Code § 33548) is provided; the text has no effective-date or other sections. Subsection (d) is printed as "d)" without the opening parenthesis, and its paragraph numbering (1), (2) follows that label; the text is otherwise quoted as provided. The text gives no underlining or marking of new versus existing language, so it is not possible to tell which parts are new from the document alone.

thresholds.note: The bill sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment of anyone. The only dates (after January 1, 2024 and after January 1, 2025) are timing triggers for when the commission considers curriculum revisions. They are procedural time limits, which the codebook codes as events, not thresholds.
